title: Leaf petiole and stem blight disease of sweet potato

Header: Leaf petiole and stem blight disease of sweet potato

Prevention: When selecting planting material, avoid using any vine cuttings with symptoms on leaves, petioles and stems.
Monitoring: Leaves: at first, small dark brown to black oval spots occur on the fully-grown leaves and show a pattern of rings.
Leaves: veins turn black on underside of leaves.
Leaves: spots grow up to 5 mm in diameter, frequently join together and are often surrounded by yellow halos.
Leaves: later, the infected leaves turn yellow and fall off.
In severe cases they create a carpet of dead blackened leaves over the soil.
Petioles and stems: spots are grey at first, later becoming black and sunken.
If they grow right around the petiole and stem they will kill them.
Direct Control: Destory vines after harvest to prevent disease spread.
